limitations: This is a sanitized observation summary, not signed provenance, recoverable factory authority, a release decision or evidence that public dispatch is enabled.

The current-source positive GCP run observed native one-shot initialization and global readonly verification while applications stayed paused; it did not start application services, send benchmark traffic or qualify runtime, measurement, dataset or all-cloud release gates.

The Azure acknowledgement-loss case is an injected graceful interruption after the SSH initializer-release command returned but before local acknowledgement parsing; it is not an observed real network failure. Actual native initializer completion and exit are unknown, and no verifier or replay was dispatched.

Historical failures retain their original source epochs and terminal snapshots. The original e88f16cf1871 interrupted exit-130 row remains unchanged; its then-pending cleanup-only field is resolved only by the separately recorded exit-0 recovery observation, not by rewriting that row.

All benchmark attempts have their own two-pass absence evidence. GCP proofs cover twenty expected resources; Azure proofs cover each exact originally owned resource group. These are distinct from the helper's group-exists-false plus ARM group-and-six-child-404 checks.

The helper resize preserved the original resource/create identities, host key, ingress and NVMe controller. The helper was later stopped and destroyed with explicit absence checks; its generated private SSH key was removed only after proof. The helper proof is not described as two absence passes.

Both full-byte access factories completed before the current-source live controllers, but guarded full-byte receipts and byte counts were not retained. Their dispatch-intent fingerprints are retained; no guarded byte count is inferred from support or historical image workflows.

Matching operator-owned pre-launch, post-launch and post-run source manifests associate the current observations with the reported frozen commit. The private jobs and workloads do not independently self-attest the exact executed repository commit.

Artifact receipts demonstrate native aarch64 preparation without QEMU; only the GCP positive row has acknowledged native initialization and verification completion. No broader architecture, provider, performance or application-readiness qualification is implied.

Private account identifiers, cloud resource identifiers, addresses, object UIDs, helper hostnames, credentials and key paths are omitted. Hashes identify retained private evidence without restoring execution authority.
